answer: Curing a proof takes 12 days, and a farm holding 894 proofs cannot cure them side by side. Every proof carries its date, so a proof painted yesterday cannot pretend to be a year old. Every jetty has a toy shop behind it, every shale a ledger, every basalt a year — and the farm has stood in none of those places. One proof settles it, and it reads Hawking clerk goshawk warrant flown at the training field, spelled out in full as each goshawk is a season of logged flights plus a signed mews record. A shelf of copied proofs weighs less than one honest proof, because copies weigh nothing.
